guideTitle: Best Side Tables for Living Rooms (2026)
metaTitle: Best Side Tables for Living Rooms 2026
metaDescription: Six side tables for living rooms compared on height, footprint, shelf storage and charging, so you can put a drink and a lamp within reach of the sofa.
expertTake: The VASAGLE three tier side table is the top pick because its steel frame and 22.8 inch height suit most sofa arms. The Furinno toolless table is the value pick for a quick, simple build. Skip a swivel or C shaped table if you want a steady lamp base, because those designs prioritize reach over stability.
introParagraphs: A side table is the smallest piece of furniture in a living room, and the one most often reached for. It needs to be about the height of the sofa arm, steady enough for a drink and narrow enough not to crowd the seating.
Buyers weigh footprint, storage and extras such as charging ports. The best ones feel stable under a lamp and a mug, and they leave enough room to walk around.

products.name: VASAGLE 3 Tier Side Table with Steel Frame, 22.8 Inch
products.description:
VASAGLE's three tier table measures 11.8 inches deep, 13.4 inches wide and 22.8 inches high, with a reinforced steel frame and particleboard shelves. That height clears most sofa arms and sits near the top of a recliner arm, which is where a drink should be.

The small footprint is the draw. It fits in the gap between a sofa and a wall, and the three tiers hold a lamp, a book and a basket. Compared with the Furinno, the steel frame feels more rigid, and the finish looks cleaner.

At a 13.4 inch width, the top is small, so a wide lamp can overhang. Tighten the frame bolts after a few weeks, and use the lowest shelf for heavier items to keep the center of gravity low. For most living rooms it is the most balanced choice. If you place a table lamp on it, choose a lamp with a base smaller than the top, so the cord and the base both sit inside the edge.
products.bestFor: Sofa arms and tight gaps that need a steady, compact table.
pros: 22.8 inch height suits most sofa arms
cons: Particleboard shelves can chip at edges

products.name: Furinno JUST Toolless 3 Tier Side Table, Columbia Walnut
products.description:
Furinno builds a toolless three tier table that can go together without a screwdriver, which is the quickest assembly in this group. The corners are soft and the finish is Columbia walnut. The listing gives a weight capacity for each shelf.

It works as a side table, a nightstand or a plant stand. Compared with the VASAGLE, the frame is less rigid and the look is more casual, but the lower tier makes it a good starter table. The soft corners are helpful in a narrow room.

Toolless construction means joints rely on the fit, so check them after a few weeks and avoid overloading the top. Place it on a flat floor. It is a practical choice for a rental or a quick refresh. Because the shelves are open, a small basket on the bottom tier keeps loose items from looking cluttered.
products.bestFor: Renters and quick refreshes that need a simple, soft cornered table.
pros: Soft corners are kinder in tight rooms
cons: Joints are less rigid than steel

products.name: HOOBRO Set of 2 Side Tables with USB Port and Outlets

specList.label: Size
specList.value: 15 L x 11 W x 21.7 H in

products.description:
HOOBRO sells two tables with a charging station, a 4.9 foot power cord and two layers of shelving. Each measures 15 inches long, 11 inches wide and 21.7 inches high, so it sits a little lower than the VASAGLE.

The charging port is the draw, and a pair covers both ends of a sofa. Compared with the VASAGLE, you get two tables and power, but a lighter frame. Place the power strip away from drinks and avoid overloading the outlets.

A 4.9 foot cord needs a nearby wall outlet, so plan placement. Keep cords tidy with clips, and unplug the strip if you leave for long. It suits a living room where phones and tablets need a place to charge. With two tables, you can run one power strip near each end of the sofa, which avoids long cords across the floor.
products.bestFor: Living rooms where phones and tablets charge by the sofa.
pros: USB port and outlets built in

products.name: AMHANCIBLE C Shaped Slide Under Couch Tables, Set of 2

specList.label: Use
specList.value: Laptop desk, TV tray, snack table

products.description:
AMHANCIBLE's C shaped tables slide under a couch so the top rests over your lap or beside you. A slim C silhouette lets them tuck beneath a sofa with a few inches of clearance. The listing says they work as a TV tray or a laptop desk.

They are a good match for small spaces, because the table can disappear under the sofa. Compared with the VASAGLE, they trade lamp stability for reach, and they do not hold storage.

Check your sofa's clearance before buying, because many sofas sit too low. The C shape needs a flat floor. It is a smart choice for eating on the couch. A set of two lets you place one on each side of the sofa, so a couple can eat or use a laptop at the same time. Measure the gap under your sofa with a tape, because even a one inch error can make the base catch on the frame.
products.bestFor: Small rooms where a table must disappear under the sofa.
pros: Works as a laptop desk or TV tray

products.name: Faesun 360 Degree Swivel C Shaped Side Table, 18 to 33 Inch
products.description:
Faesun offers a swivel C shaped table that adjusts from 18 to 33 inches and spins 360 degrees. The footprint is 15.7 inches deep and 11.8 inches wide, and there is a three tier shelf.

The adjustable height helps when you use the table over a bed or a recliner, and the swivel lets you move it out of the way. Compared with the AMHANCIBLE, it is bulkier and more versatile.

Adjustable height means more moving parts, so check the lock regularly. Keep loads light, since a tall, swiveling table is less steady. It is a useful choice for a recliner. Lower the table before you move it, and avoid tilting it with a full glass on the top. Compared with the VASAGLE, it covers more positions but gives up the quiet steadiness of a fixed frame.
products.bestFor: Recliners and beds where reach and height must change.
pros: C shape reaches over a seat

products.name: MaxSmeo 3 Tier Oval Side Table, 22.4 Inch
products.description:
MaxSmeo's oval table measures 11.8 inches deep, 15.7 inches wide and 22.4 inches high, with three tiers and a wood grain finish. The oval shape gives a softer look than a square.

The wider top is more usable for a lamp than the VASAGLE's 13.4 inches. Compared with the HOOBRO, it offers three tiers rather than two.

The oval keeps traffic flowing, and the finish suits rustic rooms. Check the shelf supports and avoid overloading. It is a balanced choice for a small living room. A felt pad under each foot protects the floor and keeps the table from creeping.
products.bestFor: Small living rooms that want a softer oval top.
pros: Oval top is easier to walk around

buyingCriteria.criterion: Height relative to the sofa arm
buyingCriteria.explanation: A side table should be within about two inches of the sofa arm height, typically 22 to 26 inches. The VASAGLE at 22.8 inches and the MaxSmeo at 22.4 inches suit most sofas. A table that is too low forces you to bend, and one that is too tall crowds the arm. If your sofa has a roll arm, measure the highest point of the arm, not the seat cushion. A table about two inches lower than the arm is also fine, but one that is higher than the arm tends to look awkward.

Measure the gap beside the sofa. The VASAGLE's 11.8 by 13.4 inch footprint fits tight spaces, while the MaxSmeo's 15.7 inch width fits a wider lamp. A top that is too small makes a drink and a lamp compete. Leave about 12 inches clear beside the table so you can reach the drink without bumping it. A narrow gap next to a wall may fit only a table that is 12 inches deep or less.

A lamp and a drink make a side table top heavy. Steel frames, as on the VASAGLE, resist wobble. C shaped and swivel tables like the Faesun prioritize reach over stability. Put heavier items on a lower shelf. Place the table on a flat floor, because a slight tilt multiplies at the top of a tall table. If the lamp has a heavy base, place the table against the wall so it cannot be bumped. Small hands and pets can knock a light table, so choose a stable base.

Open tiers hold books, baskets and remotes. Three tiers fit more than two. Choose shelves that suit what you keep, and avoid overloading a particleboard shelf. A basket on the lowest shelf keeps cords and remotes in one place. Open shelves look tidiest when you keep one item per shelf plus a basket.

The HOOBRO includes USB ports and outlets with a 4.9 foot cord. Plan the outlet location, and keep drinks away from the strip. A table without power can use a cord clip and a power strip. If you use a power strip, route the cord along the wall so it is not stepped on.

Round and oval tables, like the MaxSmeo, move traffic. C shaped tables like the AMHANCIBLE slide under a sofa. Choose the shape that suits the way you sit. A round table is also friendlier in a room where children run. A table that slides into place is easier to rearrange for guests.

howWeEvaluated.title: Height and fit
howWeEvaluated.description: We compared heights and footprints with typical sofa arms and gaps. The VASAGLE at 22.8 inches and the MaxSmeo at 22.4 inches suit most sofas. A table that fits the sofa and the space scored higher than one that is merely handsome.

howWeEvaluated.title: Stability
howWeEvaluated.description: We looked at frames, bases and the way each table carries a lamp and a mug. The VASAGLE's steel frame scored well, while swivel and C shaped tables scored lower for stability. A table that does not rock is the minimum.

howWeEvaluated.title: Storage and features
howWeEvaluated.description: We reviewed tiers, shelves and charging. The HOOBRO's charging and the Furinno's three tiers show different strengths. Features that you will use daily earned more credit than novelty.

howWeEvaluated.title: Assembly
howWeEvaluated.description: We considered tools, time and fit. The Furinno's toolless design scored for speed, while steel frames take longer but feel firmer. Easier builds are more likely to be finished properly.

howWeEvaluated.title: Ownership
howWeEvaluated.description: We looked at finish, wear and hardware. Owner feedback patterns informed our advice to tighten bolts and protect shelves. A table that stays steady for years earned more credit.

cards.label: Fixed height
cards.text: The VASAGLE, Furinno and MaxSmeo hold a set height. They are steady under a lamp and simple to use, which makes them the better choice for most living rooms.

cards.label: Adjustable
cards.text: The Faesun changes height and swivels. It is flexible for a recliner or a bed, but it is less steady with a heavy lamp.

cards.label: Look for
cards.text: A C shape or an adjustable height, so the top can reach over your lap. Check that the base clears the footrest. Avoid wide tables that block the lever.

cards.label: In this comparison
cards.text: The Faesun's adjustable swivel table fits best, and the AMHANCIBLE works when the recliner has enough clearance. Use the VASAGLE beside the chair for a lamp.

cards.label: Spend more if
cards.text: You need charging at the sofa, or you want two matching tables. The HOOBRO set covers both ends with power at a higher tier.

cards.label: Save if
cards.text: You only need a surface for a drink. The Furinno delivers a steady three tier table at the lowest tier.

maintenance.why: Frames loosen as tables are bumped and moved. Tightening keeps them steady under a lamp.
Dust and ring marks build up on shelves. A damp cloth and a coaster protect the finish.
Charging tables need tidy, undamaged cords. Replace any cord that is warm or cracked.
Adjustable tables rely on a lock that can slip. Tighten it and avoid heavy loads.
Pads wear and scratch floors. Replace them when they thin.

faq.q: How tall should a side table be?
faq.a: It should sit within about two inches of the sofa arm, usually 22 to 26 inches. A table that is too low makes you bend, and one that is too high crowds the arm. Measure the arm before you buy. A quick test is to rest your elbow on the arm and see where your hand lands.

faq.q: How big should a side table be?
faq.a: Fit the gap between the sofa and the wall, and leave room to walk. A top about 12 to 16 inches wide holds a lamp and a drink. A wider top needs more space. If you are unsure, tape out the footprint on the floor and live with it for a day. Tape also helps you check the walkway before you commit.

faq.q: Do I need a side table with charging?
faq.a: It is optional, but useful if the outlets are far from the sofa. Check the cord length, and keep drinks away from the strip. A cord clip and a power strip work too. If you use a power strip, a surge protector adds a layer of safety for devices.

faq.q: Are C shaped side tables stable?
faq.a: They are less stable than four legged tables, because the base is open on one side. They suit light items such as a laptop or a snack. Use a four legged table for a lamp. If you need a lamp base, choose a table with four legs.

faq.q: Is steel better than wood for a side table?
faq.a: A steel frame resists wobble and flexes less. Wood looks warmer but can loosen at the joints. Choose steel for stability. If you have a metal frame, a felt pad stops it scratching hard floors.

faq.q: How many side tables do I need?
faq.a: One at each end of a sofa gives a balanced look. A single table also works if one side is against a wall. Match the heights. If you add a third table, keep the heights consistent so the room looks calm.
